status: PROVED PARTIAL / LOW-ENTROPY GLOBAL-MIXTURE LINEAR-DEGREE AMPLIFICATION / AUDIT-PENDING

E_framework.reason: The unrestricted source problem is not solved; the restricted sufficient class is enlarged.

old_claim: The preceding theorem handled one bounded row-centered graphon component and gave a noisy degree window proportional to n.
new_claim: A finite global mixture of moving row-centered graphon components also has bounded noisy advantage through degree c n when component complexity is uniformly bounded, source LDA is bounded through an even ell_n tending to infinity with ell_n=o(n), and every non-null state has log inverse weight o(ell_n).
new_lemmas: Even-cycle exposure bounds every component spectral scale with a p_a^{-2/ell} penalty.
Subdegree state entropy makes that penalty 1+o(1), so fixed noise puts every component in the same subcritical regime.
A uniform moving-kernel diagram estimate gives the same c and C for every component.
Jensen on Walsh moments transfers the component bounds to the mixture.
exact_gap: The remaining gap is finite-population or sampling-without-replacement exchangeability and other non-iid latent architectures. The later counterexample remains outside the theorem.
next_attack: Replace homomorphism densities by injective homomorphism densities for a random permutation of a finite latent population and quantify the collision correction at degrees o(n).
